the discrete logarithm in the groups of elliptic curves can be solved in expected time e (log(q)n/4) for fields Fqn with n ≤ b ·log(q), and in expected time e log(q)n/2) for fields Fqi i with ni −→∞ and ni log q i −→ 0.

the discrete logarithm problems in the groups of elliptic curves of the form E/Fq i, where i ∈ N and q i is the ith prime power, can be solved in time O((q i) 1/3) (i.e., subexponentially) and in time O((log(q) i) 3/4) for any fixed a ≤ i ≤ b.

for any fixed elliptic curve over a fixed finite field, there is a constant c, depending on the curve, such that for any prime power q and any natural number n, the discrete logarithms can be computed in expected time e c · (q n)3/ 4).

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the discrete logarithm problems in elliptic curves over finite fields are subexponential in the size of the underlying field, provided the characteristic is large enough.
the discrete logarithm in elliptic curve groups over finite fields can be solved in expected time e( log(p) ), where p is the largest prime factor of the order of the elliptic curve group.

the discrete logarithm in elliptic curves over finite extension fields can be solved in a time which is bounded by e (n)3/4) · (log(q))2, where n and q are natural numbers with a · log q ≤ n ≤ b log(q), and a and b are fixed positive numbers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the discrete logarithm in the groups of points of elliptic curve over fields of small extension is easier than the discrete logarithm over the prime field.
the discrete logarithm in the groups of the rational points of elliptically twisted elliptic curves is not much harder than in the groups of elliptic curves.
the discrete logarithm over finite extension fields can be solved in expected subexponential time, which is the same as for finite fields.
